content:
Bloomberg reports that despite Apple accidentally including a demo video showcasing AirPods visual intelligence capabilities, the product is "still planned for a 2027 release." Here are the details.

"Product challenges still being resolved"

Earlier this week, Apple accidentally included a video showcasing AirPods visual intelligence capabilities in the macOS 26.7 release candidate.

Days before the video was published, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported the following in his Power On newsletter:

For years, Apple has been developing a camera-equipped version of AirPods under the codename B798. I had reported that the device was originally planned for a 2026 launch, then delayed to 2027. However, Apple has also been developing another version under the codename B790 (Apple is known for internally developing competing versions of the same product simultaneously). This B790 device appears to be further ahead in development: the product's code has appeared in iOS 27, and it is on Apple's internal roadmap, potentially debuting as early as this year.

Given that Apple accidentally included the video in the macOS 26.7 release candidate, coupled with the proximity to the company's expected iPhone launch event early next month, it appears the B790 device may be announced at that event.

However, Gurman now reports that Apple's "plans to sell camera-equipped AirPods will still push forward in 2027, despite leaked material suggesting the product could arrive sooner."

The report states:

Finally, Gurman noted that the recent leaks have further intensified controversy surrounding the device, with some users expressing opposition to camera-equipped AirPods on privacy grounds. However, he also pointed out that these cameras would be low-resolution sensors designed not for taking photos or recording video, but rather to "scan the surrounding environment and provide contextual information for the Siri digital assistant and other AI tools."

Whether this will be enough to quell criticism from those who have dubbed the product "pervert earbuds" remains to be seen until next year.
